oil.summary: Crude pulled back modestly on the session — WTI -0.78% to $90.57, Brent -0.19% to $95.34 — but the weekly picture remains explosive, with WTI up 8.62% and Brent up 6.75% as the US-Iran conflict dominates sentiment. US strikes on Iran and Iranian tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz drove the bulk of this week's war premium, with WTI briefly touching $91.80 intraday Thursday. The distillates complex is the standout outlier: US diesel hit an all-time record, surpassing 2022 highs, as middle distillate cracks surged on tightening global supply; RBOB, however, bucked the trend with a +1.41% session gain. Ukraine's continued strikes on Russian refinery infrastructure are redirecting Russian crude processing offshore, adding a secondary supply disruption layer. VP Vance's comments that Hormuz flows are near pre-war levels offered modest relief. Rosneft's CEO meanwhile argued China's buying behavior, not OPEC policy, is the true price anchor.
drivers: US-Iran military escalation and Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks sustaining a significant geopolitical war premium across crude benchmarks
Middle distillate crunch: US diesel at all-time record highs, refining cracks surging on tightening global supply exacerbated by Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries
China's crude purchasing cited as the dominant market stabilizer, with options markets pricing a 77.26% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting

gas.summary: Natural gas markets extended their gains on both sides of the Atlantic. Henry Hub edged up 1.24% on the day to $2.949/MMBtu, posting an 11.70% monthly advance. TTF outperformed sharply, adding 0.91% to €72.465/MWh and heading for a fourth consecutive weekly gain of 8.19%, with the monthly surge reaching nearly 30%. The primary driver is the Iran conflict's shadow over LNG flows through the Persian Gulf; European prices are pricing in reduced LNG availability despite ADNOC confirming it continues loading cargoes. A former Ukrainian official publicly stated the Iran war matters 'significantly more' to gas prices than the Ukraine conflict, pushing back on US Treasury Secretary Bessent's framing. On the supply-side policy front, the UK is poised to approve the Jackdaw North Sea gas field, while a Russian sanctions bill reportedly stalled in US Congress partly over concern about gas price impacts.
drivers: Iran conflict raising LNG supply-route risk through the Persian Gulf, driving TTF to a fourth straight weekly gain despite ADNOC continuing to load cargoes
European gas (TTF) surging ~30% month-on-month as markets price in sustained Middle East disruption risk and tighter LNG availability
UK Jackdaw North Sea gas field approval expected before month-end, offering a medium-term supply relief signal; US Russia sanctions bill stalled partly on gas price concerns

power.summary: The power and carbon complex was comparatively quiet today. EU EUAs ticked up just 0.04% to $79.83/EUA, with a modest 1.56% weekly gain and 3.52% monthly move — subdued relative to the volatility in gas and oil. The principal cross-market pressure point remains TTF, which feeds directly into continental power generation costs, but EUA prices are not yet reflecting the gas spike with the same intensity. On the policy front, India announced a plan to mandate battery storage at new solar and wind projects from July 2027, a structurally significant clean-power signal for the world's third-largest energy consumer. The US diesel record and broader Middle East supply squeeze are deepening the fossil fuel cost environment, but headline carbon data provided limited new information today. News flow for this sector was thin on direct power market catalysts.
drivers: EU EUAs broadly stable despite surging TTF gas prices, suggesting carbon market has not yet fully repriced the gas-driven generation cost shock
India mandating battery storage for solar and wind projects from July 2027, a significant long-term policy driver for storage demand and renewable integration
Broader Middle East conflict escalation deepening fossil fuel cost pressures, with record US diesel prices underscoring a tightening global fuel supply environment
